parts.title: Or35a: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
parts.append_markdown:
### F1-only dynamic reanalysis

A separate reanalysis of the retained F1 readings uses the supplied F1 workbook channel labels and source-cell map. For **Or35a**, the odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts are **2-heptanone: +0.62 pp; isopentyl acetate: +0.12 pp; valeric acid: +2.98 pp; pentyl acetate: +0.48 pp**. Each well is normalized to its first-three-reading mean; the contrast subtracts the matched channel’s DMSO late-to-early change from the odorant change (last-three mean / first-three mean − 1). This metric uses F1 only and is distinct from S and VUAA1-referenced N above; it does not replace those calculations or supply an independent biological replicate. VUAA1 is retained as reference data without division or threshold selection.

One well represents each condition. A positive contrast can reflect less decline than DMSO; it does not establish receptor-specific activation. The experimenter confirmed this F1 channel mapping; it supersedes the earlier Test 2 receptor labels, without changing the raw measurements. [Full F1/DoOR comparison and interpretation](https://2026.igem.wiki/nthu/results#f1-dynamic-door) · [Analysis and validation source](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/tree/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/odor-f1-dynamic).

collection.append_markdown:
### F1-only dynamics compared with DoOR

The retained Test 2 F1 records were reanalysed using each well’s first-three and last-three mean (0/12/24 s and 144/156/168 s). D = L/E − 1 and C = D_odor − D_DMSO for the same supplied channel; 100C is reported in percentage points. This F1-only metric is distinct from F0-subtracted S and VUAA1-referenced N, and is a reanalysis rather than an independent experiment. The supplied F1 workbook channel mapping and source-cell provenance are retained.

DoOR consensus minus receptor-specific spontaneous firing rate was compared with C separately for each odorant. Pearson r / Spearman rho: 2-heptanone +0.317/+0.406; isopentyl acetate +0.325/+0.442; valeric acid +0.211/+0.283; pentyl acetate −0.002/+0.006. n=10 receptors except valeric acid (n=9; missing Or42a reference). ORCO-only and blank controls are not included in tuning-OR correlations. Thus three odorants show weak positive correspondence and pentyl acetate is near zero. One well per condition and a shared vehicle reference constrain interpretation; positive C can mean less decline than DMSO. No independent replicate, significance claim, receptor-specific activation, or trained odor-classifier validation is inferred.

[Two comparison figures and full discussion](https://2026.igem.wiki/nthu/results#f1-dynamic-door). DoOR source: Münch & Galizia (2016), https://doi.org/10.1038/srep21841; DoOR.data revision 49fc21074e157327aa9aea12ba7a5024fb4b991d, CC BY-SA 4.0.
